We propose to pretrain the encoder and the de- coder of a sequence-to-sequence model under both mono- lingual and cross-lingual settings. The pre-training objective encourages the model to represent different languages in the shared space, so that we can conduct zero-shot cross-lingual transfer. After the pre-training procedure, we use monolin- gual data to ﬁne-tune the pre-trained model on downstream NLG tasks.

answer: The decoder is part of XNLG, a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence model based on Transformer [11]. Both the encoder and decoder support multiple languages, using language tag embeddings to distinguish source and target languages; conditioned on the encoding vectors and a specific target language tag, the decoder generates the output sequence in the target language [10]. The decoder is pre-trained together with the encoder using the 15-language pre-trained XLM to initialize their parameters [7], and pre-training both encoder and decoder (rather than only the encoder) is intended for cross-lingual generation tasks [12]. However, the specific architectural composition of the decoder (e.g., number of layers, attention configuration) is not specified in the provided passages.
